title_en: Classic of Mountains and Seas: The White Deer Tale
full_text_zh:
[P1] 新说山海经系列 绘本
白鹿记
文 / 张锦江 图 / 马鹏浩
华东师范大学出版社

[P3] 上申山是一座古老的大山。山下有条河，叫赤水。山间有座神庙，还有祭拜山神的地方。
有一位老人叫叔公，住在山脚的一幢五彩的石屋里。很久很久之前叔公在三十里之外的峯山，救过一头受伤的黄毛小鹿和一株被遗弃的丹木树苗。
叔公已活了一百零三岁，丹木树也长成了一株非常老的参天大树。黄毛小鹿变成了灰白色的鹿。叔公与白鹿、老树相依为命。
每天白鹿只要对着大树鸣叫一声，神树树冠就会下垂，露出一颗五彩果。叔公每日只需食五彩果一颗，便会延年益寿。白鹿只需食用树上每年只长一片的五彩叶，就有了神力。

[P4] 这一天，白鹿踩着五彩山道到河边取水给叔公和羊羔喝。谁料想，白鹿汲水时，看到渔夫老猫头为了贪捕一条巨大的鲶鱼被带下了水。

每年的三月初一，是祈求五谷丰登、祭祀山神的重要节日，上申山的山民们都要准备一百只羊羔，作为山神的祭品。
叔公家有五只羊羔，圈养在神树的树洞里。

[P5] 白鹿没有迟疑，一跃而起，踏着水面飞驰过去，救下了将死的老猫头。
落水的老猫头脸色铁青，一连数日昏迷不醒。叔公对白鹿说：“白鹿呀白鹿，救人就救到底。听祖先们说，此处往西一千两百里有一座幽都山，山头有一株蛇含草，可回魂救命，你去取来，老猫头便可得救了。”

[P6] 白鹿二话不说，轻轻一跺脚，挡在前面的山石微微一颤，天上的云朵飘了下来，白鹿跃上云朵，往西边一路翻山渡海，不消半日就来到了幽都山。

[P7] 幽都山本是一座蛇山。那蛇含草长在一条巨蛇的舌尖上。白鹿刚一踏上幽都山，就被巨蛇咬住了右腿的前蹄，巨蛇一个转身将白鹿一圈圈地缠住。
就在白鹿无法动弹而命悬一线时，巨蛇张开巨口准备将其吞下，岂料，白鹿一个扭头，将尖利如剑的鹿角刺入了巨蛇的下颚七寸处，巨蛇扭动了几下，就软瘫在幽都山脚下了。

[P8] 而白鹿也身中蛇毒，眼前一片模糊，踉跄几步后只好前蹄跪地勉强支撑着身体。此时西海翻腾起来，一个黑影从海里跃起，一只海雕冲了出来，扑向白鹿。

[P9] 白鹿口中喷出一团污血，不偏不倚喷在了海雕头上。
海雕发出一声凄厉的惨叫，坠下悬崖。此时白鹿也恢复了元气。原来那口污血正是巨蛇的毒液。

[P10] 白鹿取了巨蛇舌尖上的蛇含草，用嘴衔着，又踏云而行，翻山渡海回到了叔公的家。

[P11] 吃下蛇含草的老猫头清醒过来，他连连道谢，并承诺一定捕到赤水中最大的鲶鱼来感谢叔公。

叔公一再拒绝，无意间把神树结果和叔公、白鹿延年益寿的秘密说了出来。说者无心，听者有意，老猫头默默记在心里。

[P12] 就在老猫头离开后，山村里闯进了一头怪兽，怪兽昼伏夜出，专吃山民们用来祭祀山神的羊羔，一口一个，连吃了五日。
村里的羊渐渐少了，眼看三月初一即将到来，白鹿趁晚上月光明亮，决定去看看这头怪兽的真面目。

[P13] 说来也怪，这一看不得了，怪兽的尾巴像极了幽都山的大蛇，但冒着黑烟的身躯和头顶的独角却又不像。
怪兽见着白鹿，便两眼发光，口中喷出一个火球，差点伤到白鹿。白鹿占了下风，只好一退再退。

[P14] 白鹿一直退到了上申山
山脚下的赤水河中，后蹄掀
起了白浪，随后他埋头深深
汲了一口河水，往独角怪劈
头盖脸地喷去。

[P15] 只见独角怪在水中翻滚了几下后，冒着浓烟的身体渐渐凝固成一块岩石，突兀地立在河水中。原来是因为白鹿救老猫头时无意间踩中了岩石模样的怪兽，怪兽被惊醒了，才来山村作怪的。
白鹿击败了独角怪，
山民们欢呼庆祝。

[P16] 然而村里的头人神情凝重地对大伙说，村里的羊羔不足百只，三月初一的山神祭恐怕要误事了。山民们听了这话，就像被泼了一盆冷水，都忧心忡忡起来：得罪了山神可不是一件好事。山民们想尽办法，只勉强凑齐了九十九只羊羔，如果不能凑齐一百只羊羔，那么山神怪罪下来，就会天崩地裂，山民们一整年都不得安生。

[P17] 老猫头对头人说：“叔公家的白鹿可用作供品。”头人先是不允，这时，老猫头说出了叔公家的秘密，头人动了心，他想延年益寿，多子多孙，便派了八名壮汉随老猫头去叔公家捉白鹿。岂料神鹿不是那么好抓的。他与八个壮汉连叔公家的门也进不去，发怒的八个壮汉用石斧砍神树，砍来砍去神树完好无损。

这时，老猫头想到叔公说过，白鹿每日为他取五彩果时需要鸣叫一声。于是，他想到了一个坏主意。

[P18] 他叫人抓了一百只乌鸦，等白鹿取神果时，放出那群乌鸦，乌鸦铺天盖地地盘旋在叔公院子的上空，呱呱的叫声盖过了神鹿的鸣叫。
这天正是白鹿一年一次取食五彩叶片的时候，如不能按时取食，白鹿神力消失，就会死去。同样，叔公在这一天错过了进食神果的时辰，也会死去。于是，叔公拖着疲惫的身体，对白鹿说：“你走吧，这里容不下你了。”

[P19] 此刻，山下的鼓声响了起来，上申山最隆重的山神祭开始了。

[P20] 山民们都聚集在河滩上，山神也来了。
这是一个长得如水牛一般的神兽，它身躯硕大无比，金毛披身，头上长着弯曲上翘的角，双目闪光，飘在云端。山神说话了，声似雷鸣：
“怎么祭品只有九十九只羊呀？”显然山神发怒了。“回大神，只因前几日山里进了一头怪兽……”头人连忙伏地解释。

这时，老猫头又抢着回答：“山神息怒，因为叔公家不肯献出家中那只纯洁神圣的白鹿。”
此时忽见远处白光浮现，白鹿驮着叔公，来到山神的脚下。

[P21] 白鹿前蹄一跪，说道：“山神，我愿做第一百只祭品。”接着，叔公翻身下地也拜了拜山神，将白鹿如何救下老猫头、如何灭了独角怪守护村民和羊群、老猫头如何忘恩负义的经过一一告诉了山神。
山民们无不怒视老猫头，山神鼻孔一哼，朝老猫头吐了一口气，说：“既然此人毫无廉耻信义，也不配为人，我就将其变成——”

[P22] “羊吧！”
full_text_en:
[P1] New Tales of the Classic Mountains and Seas Series Picture Book
White Deer Chronicles
Text / Zhang Jinjiang Illustrations / Ma Penghao
East China Normal University Press

[P3] Shangshen Mountain is an ancient mountain. Below it flows a river called Chi Water. In the mountains there is a temple, and a place to worship the mountain god.
There is an old man named Shugong, who lives in a colorful stone house at the foot of the mountain. Long, long ago, Shugong rescued an injured yellow-furred fawn and a discarded Danmu sapling from Feng Mountain, thirty li away.
Shugong is now one hundred and three years old, and the Danmu tree has grown into a very old, towering tree. The yellow-furred fawn has become a gray-white deer. Shugong, the white deer, and the old tree rely on each other for survival.
Every day, when the white deer calls out to the big tree, the sacred tree's crown will droop, revealing a colorful fruit. Shugong only needs to eat one colorful fruit each day to live longer. The white deer only needs to eat the tree's colorful leaf, which grows only one per year, to gain divine power.

[P4] One day, the white deer walked along the colorful mountain path to the river to fetch water for Uncle Gong and the lambs. Unexpectedly, while drawing water, the deer saw the fisherman Old Cathead being pulled underwater in his greedy attempt to catch a huge catfish.

Every March 1st is an important festival to pray for bountiful harvests and to worship the mountain god. The mountain dwellers of Shangshen Mountain must prepare one hundred lambs as offerings to the mountain god.
Uncle Gong has five lambs, kept in the hollow of the sacred tree.

[P5] The white deer hesitated not, leapt up, and galloped across the water's surface, saving the nearly drowned Old Cathead.
Old Cathead, who had fallen into the water, had a pale, bluish face and remained unconscious for several days. Uncle Gong said to the white deer, "White deer, white deer, if we save someone, we must save them completely. According to our ancestors, a thousand and two hundred li west of here lies a mountain called Youdu. At its peak grows a plant called Shehancao, which can revive the soul and save lives. Go fetch it, and Old Cathead will be saved."

[P6] The white deer said nothing, lightly stomped its hoof, and the mountain rocks ahead trembled slightly. Clouds from the sky drifted down, and the white deer leaped onto them, journeying westward across mountains and seas, arriving at Youdu Mountain in less than half a day.

[P7] Yōudū Mountain was originally a mountain of snakes. The snake-containing herb grew on the tongue of a giant serpent. As soon as the white deer stepped onto Yōudū Mountain, it was bitten on the front hoof of its right leg by the giant snake, which then turned around and coiled the deer tightly.
Just as the white deer was unable to move and hanging by a thread, the giant snake opened its huge mouth to swallow it. Unexpectedly, the deer turned its head sharply and plunged its sharp, sword-like antler into the snake's lower jaw at the vital seven-inch point. The giant snake writhed a few times and then collapsed at the foot of Yōudū Mountain.

[P8] The white deer, poisoned by the snake, saw everything blurred. After staggering a few steps, it could only kneel on its front hooves, struggling to stay upright. At that moment, the Western Sea churned violently. A dark shadow leapt from the water, and a sea eagle burst forth, diving toward the white deer.

[P9] The white deer spat out a clump of foul blood, which landed precisely on the sea eagle's head.
The sea eagle let out a piercing cry and fell off the cliff. At this moment, the white deer also regained its strength. It turned out that the foul blood was the venom of the giant snake.

[P10] The white deer took the snake-containing herb from the tip of the giant snake's tongue, held it in its mouth, then soared on clouds, crossing mountains and seas to return to Uncle Gong's home.

[P11] The old cathead, after eating the snake-containing herb, woke up and thanked repeatedly, promising to catch the biggest catfish in the Red River to thank Uncle Gong.

Uncle Gong kept refusing, and unintentionally revealed the secret of the divine tree's fruit and how Uncle Gong and the white deer achieve longevity. The speaker meant no harm, but the listener took note—Old Cathead silently remembered it in his heart.

[P12] After Old Cathead left, a monster broke into the village. The monster hid during the day and came out at night, eating the lambs the villagers used to sacrifice to the mountain god—one by one, for five consecutive days.
As the number of sheep in the village dwindled, and with the third day of the first lunar month approaching, White Deer decided to go see the monster's true face under the bright moonlight.

[P13] Strange indeed, this creature's tail looked just like the great snake of Youdu Mountain, yet its smoky body and single horn on its head didn't quite match.
The monster saw the white deer, its eyes gleaming, and spat a fireball from its mouth, nearly hitting the deer. The white deer was at a disadvantage and could only retreat again and again.

[P14] The white deer retreated all the way to the Chi River at the foot of Shangshen Mountain. His hind hooves kicked up white waves. Then he dipped his head deep into the river, took a large gulp of water, and sprayed it right at the one-horned monster, covering it completely.

[P15] The one-horned monster rolled in the water a few times, then its smoky body gradually solidified into a rock, standing abruptly in the river. It turned out that when White Deer rescued Old Cat-Head, it accidentally stepped on the rock-like monster, awakening it and causing it to come to the village to cause trouble.
White Deer defeated the one-horned monster,
and the villagers cheered in celebration.

[P16] However, the village chief spoke gravely to everyone, saying that there were fewer than a hundred lambs in the village, and the mountain god's sacrifice on the first day of the third month might be ruined. Upon hearing this, the villagers felt as if they had been doused with a bucket of cold water, all becoming deeply anxious: offending the mountain god would be no small matter. The villagers tried every possible means, managing to gather only ninety-nine lambs. If they couldn't gather a full hundred lambs, the mountain god would be angry, causing the sky to collapse and the earth to crack, leaving the villagers unable to live in peace for the entire year.

[P17] The old cat-head said to the chief, "The white deer at Uncle's house can be used as an offering." The chief initially refused, but then the old cat-head revealed Uncle's secret. The chief became interested, wanting to live longer and have many children, so he sent eight strong men with the old cat-head to Uncle's house to catch the white deer. But the divine deer was not so easy to catch. They couldn't even enter Uncle's house, and in anger, the eight men chopped at the sacred tree with stone axes, but the tree remained unharmed.

At this moment, the old cat-head remembered that Uncle had said the white deer needed to call out once every day when fetching the colorful fruits. So, he came up with a bad idea.

[P18] He had people catch a hundred crows, and when the white deer came to fetch the sacred fruit, he released them. The crows swarmed the sky above Uncle's courtyard, their cawing drowning out the deer's call.
This was the day once a year when the white deer had to eat the colorful leaves. If it failed to eat on time, its divine power would vanish and it would die. Likewise, if Uncle missed the time to eat the sacred fruit, he too would die. So, Uncle, exhausted, said to the white deer: "Go away, there's no room for you here."

[P19] At this moment, the drums below the mountain began to sound, and the most solemn mountain god sacrifice of Shangshen Mountain began.

[P20] The villagers had gathered on the riverbank, and the mountain god had arrived.
This was a divine beast as large as a water buffalo, with a massive body, golden fur, curved horns pointing upward, and glowing eyes, floating in the clouds. The mountain god spoke, his voice like thunder:
"Why are there only ninety-nine sheep as offerings?" Clearly, the mountain god was angry. "Your Majesty, it's because a monster entered the mountains a few days ago..." the chief hurriedly explained, bowing to the ground.

At that moment, Old Cat-Head quickly replied, "Mountain God, please calm down. It's because Uncle Gong's family refuses to sacrifice their pure and sacred white deer."
Suddenly, a white light appeared in the distance, and the white deer, carrying Uncle Gong, arrived at the feet of the mountain god.

[P21] The white deer knelt on its front hooves and said, "Mountain God, I am willing to be the hundredth sacrifice." Then, Uncle Gong got up from the ground and bowed to the Mountain God, telling him in detail how the white deer had saved Old Cat-Head, how it had defeated the one-horned monster to protect the villagers and their flock, and how Old Cat-Head had betrayed its kindness.
All the villagers glared angrily at Old Cat-Head. The Mountain God sniffed through his nostrils, blew a breath toward Old Cat-Head, and said, "Since this person has no shame or integrity, and is unworthy to be human, I will turn him into——"

[P22] "Sheep, then!"
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《白鹿记》的封面，展示了书名、作者、绘者及出版社信息，画面描绘了一个古朴的村落场景，有房屋、人群、动物和飞鸟，充满山海经风格的奇幻色彩。
[P2] 本页为绘本《白鹿记》的封面，画面中央是书名“白鹿记”，左侧为一位披着绿斗篷、手持木杖的老人与一只白色小鹿，右侧竖排标注作者“文／张锦江 图／马麟浩”。下方排列四个圆形小图，描绘了老人与白鹿在不同场景中的互动，包括村落、树下、阳光下的树以及夜晚的树，整体风格充满山海经式的奇幻色彩。
[P3] 本页介绍了上申山的地理环境和一位名叫叔公的老人，他与一只白鹿和一棵神树相依为命，通过白鹿鸣叫唤醒神树结出五彩果和五彩叶，从而获得延年益寿和神力。
[P4] 本页描述了白鹿为叔公和羊羔取水时，意外目睹渔夫老猫头因贪捕巨鲶鱼而落水的场景，并介绍了三月初一祭祀山神的习俗及叔公家饲养羊羔的情况。
[P5] 白鹿跃入水中救起落水的渔夫老猫头，叔公见状，嘱咐白鹿前往一千两百里外的幽都山寻找能回魂救命的蛇含草。
[P6] 白鹿遵照叔公的嘱托，踏云翻山渡海，迅速前往一千两百里外的幽都山寻找蛇含草。
[P7] 白鹿抵达幽都山后，遭遇巨蛇袭击，被咬住前蹄并缠绕，危急时刻用鹿角刺中巨蛇七寸，使其瘫倒于山脚下。
[P8] 白鹿被巨蛇咬伤中毒，身体虚弱，正艰难支撑时，西海翻腾，一只海雕从海中冲出，扑向白鹿。
[P9] 白鹿被巨蛇咬伤后，喷出毒液击中扑来的海雕，使其坠崖，白鹿因此恢复元气。
[P10] 白鹿从巨蛇口中取得蛇含草后，踏云翻山渡海，返回叔公的家。
[P11] 老猫头服下蛇含草后苏醒，向叔公道谢并承诺捕大鲶鱼报恩；叔公拒绝时无意透露了神树果实与延年益寿的秘密，老猫头暗中记下。
[P12] 山村里出现一头怪兽，专吃祭祀山神的羊羔，白鹿决定在月圆之夜探查其真面目。
[P13] 白鹿在月圆之夜探查怪兽时，遭遇其喷火攻击，因处于下风而被迫连连后退。
[P14] 白鹿退至上申山脚下的赤水河中，汲取河水后向独角怪喷射，试图反击。
[P15] 白鹿用河水击败了喷火的独角怪，怪兽化为岩石沉入河中，村民们欢呼庆祝胜利。
[P16] 村里因羊羔不足百只，担心三月初一的山神祭无法如期举行，村民忧心忡忡，生怕得罪山神会招致天崩地裂的灾祸。
[P17] 老猫头向头人提议用白鹿作供品，头人动心后派八名壮汉去捉鹿，但神鹿难以捕捉，壮汉们甚至砍伐神树也无果。老猫头想起白鹿每日取果需鸣叫，于是萌生了一个坏主意。
[P18] 老猫头派人抓了一百只乌鸦，在白鹿取神果时放出，用乌鸦的叫声掩盖白鹿的鸣叫，导致白鹿无法按时取食神果。叔公因错过进食神果的时辰，身体疲惫，无奈让白鹿离开。
[P19] 山下的鼓声响起，上申山最隆重的山神祭正式开始，村民们聚集在山脚下举行祭祀活动。
[P20] 山神降临河滩，因祭品不足九十九只羊而发怒，头人解释是因山中怪兽作祟。老猫头趁机指责叔公不肯献出白鹿，此时白鹿驮着叔公现身于山神脚下。
[P21] 白鹿自愿成为第一百只祭品，叔公向山神讲述白鹿的功绩和老猫头的忘恩负义，山神愤怒地准备惩罚老猫头。
[P22] 一只巨大的手指向一只被烟雾环绕的羊，似乎在做出决定或提议。
[P23] 画面描绘了一棵枯树和一座小屋，背景是淡蓝色的天空，整体氛围宁静而略带荒凉，可能象征着故事中某种失落或转变后的景象。
